findings.reason: the node either hits a scope blocker or silently deviates, and the section must add the call site to its write paths or name the pointer read.
findings.text: §7 makes `_require_gate_log_agrees` read "the fresh manifest's `after_suite` arm", but that function's signature is `(run_id, gate_check, *, verdict)` and its only production caller (`reckon/crew/promotion.py:573`, inside `_require_independently`) passes no record, while the declared write paths are `reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py` and the new test — so a literal implementation must either edit the caller outside its write scope or invent an undeclared pointer re-read from `run_id`

findings.reason: without the direction stated the case is unsatisfiable for one argument order, and the node would either weaken the shared rule or report a blocker.
findings.text: §7's third case requires "a receipt whose ids differ only in a qualified versus bare test name is accepted under §5's rule", but the rule §2 defines is asymmetric (a bare base name matches a qualified head id; "a qualified id matches only the same qualified id"), and §7 never says which side carries the bare name, so the natural order of `failure_ids_covered(receipt_ids, log_ids)` refuses a qualified receipt against a bare log id

findings.reason: a control that cannot accept its case cannot show the run-selection guard fires; it must name the run selection itself, which changes both clauses.
findings.text: §7's second negative control, "reading the first run's summary instead of the last accepts the first case", mutates only the count's source, while the deliverable reads the ids from the log's last run through a separate reader, so the ids comparison still refuses the case and the control cannot produce the outcome it claims
